videos.script: The last lesson was where files live. This one is the assumption underneath it, which is that they will still be there tomorrow. {{there}} Four things take data away, and they are genuinely different problems: you delete something, a drive fails, the machine is stolen or the flat floods, and something encrypts or corrupts the files while they are still in front of you. Any arrangement that answers three of the four leaves the fourth open, and the fourth is usually the one that happens. {{four}} The sentence this lesson exists to hand over is that synchronising is not backing up. A sync service copies whatever is there, including a deletion and including a file that was encrypted a second ago, and it copies it within seconds. That is a feature, and it is not a safety net. {{sync}} So we do the rule that answers all four, what actually has to be copied, how many versions are enough, and the test that almost nobody performs. {{rule}} And we finish on documents that have to outlive the program that made them.
